-wrap break-words">If we set aside the time crunch and focus purely on a hi=
gh-impact concept that perfectly aligns with the judging criteria=E2=80=94m=
eaningful Walrus integration, heavy utilization of Tatum's Sui infrastructu=
re, and real-world utility=E2=80=94we need a concept where data decentraliz=
ation isn't just a feature, but the entire backbone of the solution.
A powerful concept that fits this mold is a **Decentralized, Compliant Medi=
cal Data Exchange (MedShare)**.
Medical record management is notoriously fragmented, fraught with privacy l=
eaks, and highly regulated. Building a platform that solves this utilizing =
Sui, Walrus, and Tatum hits every single requirement beautifully.
### The Concept: MedShare
An on-chain access management system paired with off-chain decentralized st=
orage for sensitive medical records, medical imaging (DICOM files), and res=
earch data.
### How It Works &amp; Solves the Problem
Patients own their medical records. Instead of hospital databases silo-ing =
this data, encrypted medical files are stored as immutable "blobs" on Walru=
s. Access control is managed via Sui smart contracts. When a patient visits=
 a new doctor or joins a clinical trial, they grant time-bound cryptographi=
c access to their data.
### Mapping to the Hackathon Criteria
#### 1. Meaningful Walrus Integration (30%)
Medical data=E2=80=94especially MRI scans, X-rays, and detailed patient his=
tory PDFs=E2=80=94is far too heavy to store directly on-chain.
 * **The Walrus Use Case:** It acts as the high-throughput, low-cost decent=
ralized storage layer for these large data blobs.
 * **The Technical Link:** The Sui smart contract only stores the Walrus Bl=
ob ID and a hash of the encrypted file. Walrus ensures the data is highly a=
vailable and cryptographically verifiable without exposing the actual healt=
h data to the public ledger.
#### 2. Tatum Sui RPC Infrastructure (30%)
A medical application requires real-time responsiveness and deep data index=
ing.
 * **The Tatum Use Case:** You would use Tatum=E2=80=99s enterprise-grade S=
ui RPC endpoints to listen for on-chain authorization events (e.g., a patie=
nt revoking or granting access to a doctor).
 * **The Technical Link:** Tatum=E2=80=99s Data APIs can index patient tran=
saction histories, showing a clean audit trail of exactly who has accessed =
their medical records over time=E2=80=94crucial for compliance frameworks l=
ike HIPAA or GDPR.
#### 3. Innovation &amp; Value Proposition (20%)
It directly solves a multi-billion dollar problem: interoperability in heal=
thcare. It eliminates duplicate medical testing, secures patient data again=
st ransomware attacks (which target centralized hospital servers), and give=
s users absolute sovereignty over their health history.
#### 4. Optional: Tatum MCP (AI Feature Bonus)
If you wanted to leverage the Tatum MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for=
 AI, you could feed the anonymized metadata or structured medical text file=
s retrieved from Walrus into a localized AI model. The AI could provide pat=
ients with a "plain English" summary of their complex lab results or assist=
 researchers in scanning thousands of Walrus-stored medical journals for sp=
ecific symptom correlations.
### Architectural Layout
To visualize how these pieces interact, the flow of data and authorization =
moves through distinct layers:
 1. **Frontend / App Layer:** The doctor or patient interacts with the dash=
board.
 2. **Infrastructure Layer (Tatum):** Routes transactions to the Sui networ=
k and fetches historical access logs seamlessly.
 3. **Smart Contract Layer (Sui):** Validates permissions, checks signature=
s, and matches the user's public key with the requested file metadata.
 4. **Decentralized Storage Layer (Walrus):** Streams the encrypted heavy d=
ata files back to the authorized viewer once the smart contract clears the =
permission.
What do you think about this direction? If you wanted to scale the scope ba=
ck down to something achievable for a prototype, we could easily strip away=
 the UI and focus purely on a clean backend CLI or a core smart-contract-to=

.7]">This is a genuinely strong concept. The mapping to the judging criteri=
a is tight, and medical data is one of the few domains where decentralized =
storage stops being a "nice to have" and becomes the actual thesis. Let me =
give you my honest read on it.</p>
<hr class=3D"border-border-200 border-t-0.5 my-3 mx-1.5">
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]"><strong>What's working really well</strong></p>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">The Walrus fit is probably the best I've seen for this kind of subm=
ission. DICOM files (MRI/CT scans) routinely run 50=E2=80=93500MB each. Sto=
ring blob IDs on-chain while the heavy payload lives on Walrus isn't just a=
rchitecturally sound =E2=80=94 it's <em>the correct solution</em> to a real=
 constraint. Judges who understand the stack will recognize that immediatel=
y.</p>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">The audit trail angle via Tatum's indexing is also sharp. HIPAA com=
pliance is fundamentally a logging and access-accountability problem. Frami=
ng Tatum's Data APIs as your compliance layer rather than just "an RPC endp=
oint" elevates the integration from infrastructure to product feature. That=
's the right mental model.</p>
<hr class=3D"border-border-200 border-t-0.5 my-3 mx-1.5">
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]"><strong>The honest risks</strong></p>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">The concept is <em>wide</em>. A full MedShare platform with patient=
 dashboards, doctor portals, DICOM streaming, and AI summaries is probably =
a 3-month build for a team. For a solo prototype by June 8th, you need to b=
e ruthless about what the demo actually shows.</p>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">There's also a subtle framing risk: judges may mentally bucket this=
 as "another healthcare dApp concept" and discount it as vaporware unless t=
he working demo is undeniably concrete. The idea needs to <em>run</em>, not=
 just be described.</p>
<hr class=3D"border-border-200 border-t-0.5 my-3 mx-1.5">
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]"><strong>The prototype strip-down I'd actually recommend</strong></p=
>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">Focus the submission on the <strong>core permission pipeline</stron=
g> =E2=80=94 the thing that makes the whole concept real. Everything else i=
s UI polish on top of this:</p>

<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">That's the entire value proposition in one demonstrable flow. Build=

and a real Tatum RPC call. That's more compelling than a half-built UI.</p>
<hr class=3D"border-border-200 border-t-0.5 my-3 mx-1.5">
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]"><strong>The AI bonus angle =E2=80=94 do it or skip it cleanly</stro=
ng></p>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">If you add it, make it do exactly one thing well: take a retrieved =
Walrus blob (a structured lab result JSON or PDF), pass it through the Tatu=
m MCP, and return a plain-English summary. Don't over-scope it. If it feels=
 rushed, leave it out entirely =E2=80=94 a tight 4-layer demo beats a bloat=
ed 5-layer one with a broken AI feature.</p>
<hr class=3D"border-border-200 border-t-0.5 my-3 mx-1.5">
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]"><strong>My verdict</strong></p>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">This concept is worth building. The Walrus integration is genuinely=
 meaningful (not cosmetic), the Tatum usage maps to a real product need, an=
d the problem domain has undeniable real-world weight. The risk isn't the i=
dea =E2=80=94 it's scope management.</p>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=

load flow for the prototype? That's the critical path item to nail first, a=

 grid-cols-1 grid [&amp;_&gt;_*]:min-w-0 gap-3 font-claude-response"><h1 cl=
ass=3D"text-text-100 mt-3 -mb-1 text-[1.375rem] font-bold">=F0=9F=8F=A5 Med=
Share =E2=80=94 Decentralized Medical Data Exchange</h1>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">A decentralized platform for secure medical record management, buil=
t on <strong>Sui</strong> + <strong>Walrus</strong> + <strong>Tatum</strong=
>. Patients own their health data. Encrypted medical files are stored as im=
mutable blobs on Walrus, while access control and audit trails are managed =
on-chain via Tatum's Sui RPC infrastructure.</p>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">Built for the <a class=3D"underline underline underline-offset-2 de=
coration-1 decoration-current/40 hover:decoration-current focus:decoration-=
current" href=3D"https://tatum.io/tatum-x-walrus-hackathon">Tatum x Walrus =
Hackathon</a>.</p>
<hr class=3D"border-border-200 border-t-0.5 my-3 mx-1.5">
<h2 class=3D"text-text-100 mt-3 -mb-1 text-[1.125rem] font-bold">The Proble=
m</h2>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">Healthcare data is fragmented across siloed hospital databases, cre=
ating three critical failures:</p>
<ul class=3D"[li_&amp;]:mb-0 [li_&amp;]:mt-1 [li_&amp;]:gap-1 [&amp;:not(:l=
ast-child)_ul]:pb-1 [&amp;:not(:last-child)_ol]:pb-1 list-disc flex flex-co=
l gap-1 pl-8 mb-3">
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>No interoperability</strong> =E2=80=94 patients repeat tests when s=
witching providers because records don't transfer</li>
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Ransomware targets</strong> =E2=80=94 centralized hospital servers =
are the #1 target for healthcare cyberattacks</li>
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Zero patient sovereignty</strong> =E2=80=94 patients have no contro=
l over who accesses their medical history</li>
</ul>
<h2 class=3D"text-text-100 mt-3 -mb-1 text-[1.125rem] font-bold">The Soluti=
on</h2>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">MedShare replaces centralized medical databases with a trust-minimi=
zed architecture:</p>

ope=3D"col" class=3D"text-text-100 border-b-0.5 border-[hsl(var(--border-30=

strong>Tatum Data API</strong></td><td class=3D"border-b-0.5 border-[hsl(va=
r(--border-300)/0.3)] py-2 pr-4 align-top">Real-time transaction indexing a=
nd compliance-grade audit logs</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">Patients grant and revoke time-bound cryptographic access to doctor=
s. Every access event is logged immutably. Medical files never touch a cent=
ralized server.</p>

<h2 class=3D"text-text-100 mt-3 -mb-1 text-[1.125rem] font-bold">Walrus Int=
egration</h2>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">Medical data =E2=80=94 MRI scans, X-rays, lab results =E2=80=94 is =
far too heavy for on-chain storage. Walrus provides the decentralized blob =
storage layer:</p>
<ul class=3D"[li_&amp;]:mb-0 [li_&amp;]:mt-1 [li_&amp;]:gap-1 [&amp;:not(:l=
ast-child)_ul]:pb-1 [&amp;:not(:last-child)_ol]:pb-1 list-disc flex flex-co=
l gap-1 pl-8 mb-3">
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Upload</strong>: Encrypted patient records are stored as immutable =
blobs via the Walrus Publisher HTTP API (<code class=3D"bg-text-200/5 borde=
r border-0.5 border-border-300 text-danger-000 whitespace-pre-wrap rounded-=
[0.4rem] px-1 py-px text-[0.9rem]">PUT /v1/blobs</code>)</li>
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Retrieval</strong>: Authorized parties fetch blobs via the Walrus A=
ggregator (<code class=3D"bg-text-200/5 border border-0.5 border-border-300=
 text-danger-000 whitespace-pre-wrap rounded-[0.4rem] px-1 py-px text-[0.9r=
em]">GET /v1/blobs/{blobId}</code>)</li>
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Verification</strong>: Only the Blob ID and file hash are stored on=
 Sui =E2=80=94 the actual data never touches the public ledger</li>
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Availability</strong>: Walrus erasure coding ensures data remains r=
etrievable even with partial node failures</li>
</ul>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">The Sui smart contract stores only the Walrus Blob ID and a SHA-256=
 hash of the encrypted file, keeping on-chain costs minimal while maintaini=
ng cryptographic verifiability.</p>
<h2 class=3D"text-text-100 mt-3 -mb-1 text-[1.125rem] font-bold">Tatum Inte=
gration</h2>
<p class=3D"font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading=
-[1.7]">Tatum provides the enterprise-grade infrastructure layer connecting=
 MedShare to Sui:</p>
<ul class=3D"[li_&amp;]:mb-0 [li_&amp;]:mt-1 [li_&amp;]:gap-1 [&amp;:not(:l=
ast-child)_ul]:pb-1 [&amp;:not(:last-child)_ol]:pb-1 list-disc flex flex-co=
l gap-1 pl-8 mb-3">
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Sui RPC Gateway</strong>: All on-chain transactions (metadata regis=
tration, access control state changes) are routed through Tatum's Sui RPC e=
ndpoints with API key authentication</li>
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Transaction Building</strong>: Gas price fetching (<code class=3D"b=
g-text-200/5 border border-0.5 border-border-300 text-danger-000 whitespace=
-pre-wrap rounded-[0.4rem] px-1 py-px text-[0.9rem]">suix_getReferenceGasPr=
ice</code>), coin management (<code class=3D"bg-text-200/5 border border-0.=
5 border-border-300 text-danger-000 whitespace-pre-wrap rounded-[0.4rem] px=
-1 py-px text-[0.9rem]">suix_getCoins</code>), and transaction execution al=
l flow through Tatum</li>
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Data API</strong>: Patient transaction histories are indexed via Ta=
tum's account API, providing a compliance-ready audit trail showing exactly=
 who accessed what records and when</li>
<li class=3D"font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">=
<strong>Rate Limit Handling</strong>: Built-in retry logic with exponential=
 backoff for production reliability</li>
</ul>

@keyframes spin {=20
  100% { transform: rotate(360deg); }
}

@keyframes ping {=20
  75%, 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(2); }
}

@keyframes pulse {=20
  50% { opacity: 0.5; }
}

@keyframes fade {=20
  0% { opacity: 0; }
  100% { opacity: 1; }
}

@keyframes zoom {=20
  0% { transform: scale(0.95); }
  100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes accordion-open {=20
  0% { opacity: 0; height: 0px; }
  100% { height: var(--radix-accordion-content-height); opacity: 1; }
}

@keyframes accordion-close {=20
  0% { height: var(--radix-accordion-content-height); opacity: 1; }
  100% { opacity: 0; height: 0px; }
}

@keyframes shimmer {=20
  0% { transform: translate(-100%); }
  60% { transform: translate(100%); }
  100% { transform: translate(100%); }
}

@keyframes shimmertext {=20
  0% { background-position: 100% 0px; }
  65% { background-position: 0px 0px; }
  100% { background-position: 0px 0px; }
}

@keyframes blink {=20
  0%, 100% { opacity: 1; }
  50% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes pulse-dot {=20
  0%, 100% { transform: scale(0.75); }
  50% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@font-face { font-family: Anthropicons-Variable; src: url("https://assets-p=
roxy.anthropic.com/claude-ai/v2/assets/v1/c0f671921-CWuQ-ElP.woff2") format=
("woff2-variations"); font-weight: 400 700; font-display: block; }

@keyframes dframe-dot-pulse {=20
  0%, 5% { opacity: 0.3; animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.8=
4, 0.44, 1); }
  15%, 25% { opacity: 1; animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.8=
4, 0.44, 1); }
  65%, 100% { opacity: 0.3; }
}

.dframe-dot { width: 2px; height: 2px; border-radius: 9999px; background: h=
sl(var(--text-400)); animation: 1.8s linear 0s infinite normal none running=
 dframe-dot-pulse; }

.dframe-dot:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.2s; }

.dframe-dot:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 0.4s; }

@keyframes check-spin-in {=20
  0% { transform: translateY(8px) rotate(-270deg) scale(0); }
  100% { transform: translateY(0px) rotate(0deg) scale(1); }
}

.check-spin-in { animation: 0.33s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) 0s 1 normal =
both running check-spin-in; }

:root { --dot-ready: hsl(210 80% 55%); --dot-awaiting: var(--extended-yello=
w); }

[data-mode=3D"dark"] { --dot-ready: hsl(210 85% 65%); }

.status-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; position: relati=
ve; display: block; }

.status-dot[data-kind=3D"ready"] { background: var(--dot-ready); }

.status-dot[data-kind=3D"awaiting"] { background: var(--dot-awaiting); }

@keyframes dframe-dot-blink {=20
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0.3; }
  50% { opacity: 1; }
}

.status-dot[data-kind=3D"running"] { background: hsl(var(--text-400)); anim=
ation: 1.2s ease-in-out 0s infinite normal none running dframe-dot-blink; }

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .dframe-dot, .check-spin-in, .status-dot[data-kind=3D"running"] { animati=
on: auto ease 0s 1 normal none running none; }
}

@keyframes timeline-fade-in {=20
  0% { opacity: 0; }
  100% { opacity: 1; }
}

@keyframes timeline-collapse {=20
  0% { grid-template-rows: 1fr; opacity: 1; }
  100% { grid-template-rows: 0fr; opacity: 0; }
}

.timeline-block-fade-exit { animation: 0.15s ease-out 0s 1 normal forwards =
running timeline-fade-out; }

@keyframes timeline-fade-out {=20
  0% { opacity: 1; }
  100% { opacity: 0; }
}

.timeline-block-exit { display: grid; overflow: hidden; animation: 0.1s eas=
